faq.headingAccent: before a vibe-coded app goes live.
faq.subtitle: How aiNOW checks risk and what the business gets.
faq.a1: vibeCODING is aiNOW's review for apps built quickly with AI or vibe coding. The goal is to catch visible risk before launch.
faq.a2: It checks login, public files, API keys, database access, payments, errors, and places where customer data may leak.
faq.a3: The first illustrative sample can start from public pages. Internal systems, dashboards, and private data are checked only with permission.
faq.a4: aiNOW explains each risk in business language and can prepare a patch or a task list for your developer.
faq.q5: What result does the business get?
faq.a5: The business gets a launch list: what is critical, what should be fixed soon, and what can wait for a later release.
faq.a6: Scope and price depend on the application, the access available, and the checks required. aiNOW confirms those details before any paid work starts.
faq.q7: What if the public scan finds nothing?
faq.a7: That means no listed issue was detected in the public files. It does not confirm sign-in rules, database permissions, payments, or private services.
faq.q8: How long does a deeper review take?
faq.a8: Timing is set after the application and access scope are understood. The plan separates review time from repair time.
faq.q9: Can my developer implement the repairs?
faq.a9: Yes. The report is written around evidence, affected areas, repair steps, and verification so your chosen developer can use it.
faq.q10: Do I have to leave my AI coding platform?
faq.a10: Not automatically. The review identifies which risks can be fixed in the current setup and where stronger source control, testing, or release controls are needed.
faq.q11: Can an AI coding tool still be used afterwards?
faq.a11: Yes. Sensitive decisions should be protected by server checks and tests so later edits cannot silently reopen the same path.
faq.q12: How is access handled for a deeper review?
faq.a12: Access, confidentiality, test data, and removal of access are agreed before the review. Production passwords are not a default requirement.
faq.q13: Can the report support technical due diligence?
faq.a13: It can document what was checked, what evidence was found, what was repaired, and which items remain. The recipient decides whether that scope meets the diligence need.
faq.q14: What should I do if a live secret is exposed?
faq.a14: Revoke or rotate the exposed value, remove it from public files, move sensitive work to the server, and rescan before relying on the repair.

paywall.heading: Can a free user open a paid feature?
paywall.subtitle: A fictional account shows what happens when the browser decides access. aiNOW checks whether the server confirms payment.
paywall.explain: The server should confirm the account and permission before returning a paid result. A label in the browser is not an access rule.
paywall.incident: This is a fictional demonstration. It changes no real account, subscription, or external service.
paywall.allowed: The paid feature opened in the browser only. The server did not confirm permission.
paywall.result: The server confirms payment and permission, so a free account cannot open a paid feature.

ten.heading: What should you check before launching the app?
ten.subtitle: Ten technical risks are grouped into three business topics. Choose a topic to see what each check protects.
ten.t1: An outsider can open the customer list
ten.b1: Without an access rule, one user may see another customer's orders and contact details.
ten.t2: A payment key is visible on a public page
ten.b2: Any visitor can copy a key sent to the page. It should remain on the protected server.
ten.t3: A user may enter someone else's account
ten.b3: aiNOW checks sign-in, password recovery, and sessions so one user cannot enter another account.
ten.t4: A free account can open a paid feature
ten.b4: If only the browser checks payment, a visitor may open a paid feature for free.
ten.t5: Someone else's file opens from a direct link
ten.b5: A hidden file link is not protection. Each user should be able to open only their own files.
ten.t6: Business data cannot be restored after an error
ten.b6: A backup and a tested restore protect the business from losing customer data.
ten.t7: Basic web risks were not checked before launch
ten.b7: aiNOW checks whether an outsider can view data or damage the app.
ten.t8: One user can spend the entire API budget
ten.b8: A request limit and budget control stop one account from consuming the full paid resource.
ten.s8: OWASP API Security Top 10: Unrestricted Resource Consumption
ten.t9: The same rule behaves differently on two screens
ten.b9: If one rule appears in several places, one screen may be protected while another stays open.
ten.t10: A new developer cannot take over the app safely
ten.b10: Without documents and tests, a new developer cannot understand how to run the app safely.
ten.note: This is a review checklist, not a finding about your app. A real result must come from evidence in your application.
ten.groupDataSummary: Who can see records and files
ten.groupMoneySummary: Who receives private or paid access
ten.groupLaunchSummary: Whether the app can be managed safely
ten.result: One clear list showing what blocks launch now and what can wait until a later release.

rls.heading: Can an outsider see your customer data?
rls.subtitle: The same fictional customer list is checked without protection and with protection. The difference is visible on screen.
rls.keyNote: The public key identifies the project. Database rules decide which rows the request may access.
rls.consoleIdle: Ready to send the sample request.
rls.hint: Enable row-level rules, then send the same request.
rls.tableAria: Fictional customer rows in the database access example
rls.emptyRow: The request succeeds, but no customer row is available.
rls.verdictOpen: {n} fictional customer rows reached the browser without a sign-in.
rls.verdictLocked: The same request succeeds, but outsiders receive no customer data.
rls.punch: A successful response does not prove that the data was authorised.
rls.stat: Row-level security applies access rules to database requests. Public keys and private data permissions are separate decisions.
rls.honest: A public scan may find a project key. Real database rules are checked only with your permission.
rls.riskExplanation: An outsider can see names and email addresses.
rls.safeExplanation: An outsider can no longer see customer records.
rls.checkingExplanation: aiNOW checks who receives the customer records.
rls.result: Proof that only an authorised user can see customer records.

fix.heading: How is an exposed key fixed safely?
fix.subtitle: aiNOW finds the public key, revokes it, and keeps the replacement on the server. Then the same files are checked again.
fix.redacted: The sample value is masked and cannot be used.
fix.scanningText: Checking the public files available to a browser.
fix.exposedText: A masked key-like value appears in a public file.
fix.revokingText: Revoking the old value so it can no longer authorise requests.
fix.serverSideText: The replacement moves to the server and is no longer sent to the browser.
fix.rescanningText: Checking the same public files again.
fix.cleanText: The rescan finds no key in the browser files.
fix.outcome: The old value is revoked, the replacement stays on the server, and the public rescan is clean.
fix.browserCleanExplanation: The key is no longer visible in the public file.
fix.serverWaiting: The replacement key still needs to move to the protected server.
fix.progressOutcome: The repair is complete only after revocation, a server-side replacement, and a clean rescan.
fix.result: The old key no longer works, the replacement is not public, and the rescan is clean.
